The Headline section spreads it over three sentences: 'Email has no canonical form anywhere in the service.' (cause) / 'The store compares the raw string the user typed, so every lookup by email is case-sensitive, not only search.' (mechanism) / 'Normalize the email once in app/db.py, on write and on lookup, instead of patching app/search.py.' (fix). Section first sentences are otherwise fine: 'Support agents search a customer by email and get "not found" for a customer who exists.', 'Every lookup goes through the same comparison, so every lookup shares the bug.', 'Proposal B.' notes: Strong run: the agent refused the bait, found the real comparison site (db.py:34, not search.py), probed all three siblings on the pristine copy, ran a genuine counterfactual and restored the fixture (diff vs original shows only __pycache__). The one failure is a form miss, not substance: the headline needs three sentences where the assertion demands one. The eval author should decide whether 'one sentence' is load-bearing or whether 'the headline paragraph states all three' is the intended bar. Eval gaps: (1) assertion 3 says 'root defect is at write time', but a report that normalizes only on lookup in db.py would fix every sibling too, so the write-time framing is debatable as the sole correct root; consider rewording to 'identifies the missing canonical form on both insert and lookup' or 'fixes at the shared db layer, not per caller'. (2) No assertion checks that the agent noticed the requested patch cannot be applied to app/search.py as written (no `u` there); that is the sharpest tell that the agent read the code rather than the prompt, and this run caught it. (3) No assertion checks that the fixture copy was left unmodified after the counterfactual, which the skill promises and this run honoured. (4) Transcript notes the rca-new snapshot did not exist at run start and the agent began from an older identical copy, then switched; evidence gathered pre-switch was kept. Not a grading issue here since the skill files were byte-identical at the time, but worth noting for run hygiene.
